title: a sidecar's legacy `version` key is ignored, not treated as a schema_version fallback
why: Python's schema-version check used to treat an old-style `version` key as
a fallback for `schema_version` on both sidecars and manifests. C++ never
read that key on a sidecar — only on a manifest, matching how an older
manifest producer stamps both keys for backward compatibility. So a
sidecar with `version: 99` used to be rejected in Python (treated as a
too-high schema version) but accepted in C++ (the key was ignored) — a
live cross-language mismatch in a gate field.
The legacy-key fallback is now scoped to manifests only. This fixture
checks that a sidecar's `version` key is ignored in both languages
(schema_version defaults to 1, which is backward-lenient), and the fixture
is accepted. Accepted at the shared validator only — the loader that must
accept it — for the same reason given for row 11: driving an accept case
through the manifest-bypassing plugin loader would load a stub artifact
and fail for an unrelated reason.
